The years in me have always dreamt of being shed, so now is the time of their rejoicing. With insuperable, beastly gumption, it is proclaimed by the immortal silence between two fulsome heart beats, that the time of life is but the garment of life eternal. I can wear the years proudly now, knowing myself to be more than the sum of their trends, for I sit and know my nakedness, now as always apparently, and about me hang freely the stylings of these days, tenderly collected. After a fashion, I let this time be, cradled in the stories that vanish in the unglamorous light of beatific wakefulness.
